newsitem.title: INDIA: India sugar prices up sharply as govt lowers quota.
newsitem.headline: India sugar prices up sharply as govt lowers quota.

text.p: Indian sugar prices on Wednesday rose sharply following a lower than expected free sale quota announced by the government for next month, dealers said.
The free sale quota for April is 700,000 tonnes, down from market expectations of 750,000 tonnes and against 700,000 tonnes this month. The quota in April 1996 was 660,000 tonnes.
"The announcement of a lower than expected quota triggered speculative buying in the ready delivery while offerings were limited by the millers," a dealer said.
In ready delivery sugar S-30 moved up by 5/22 rupees at 1,290/1,310 rupees per quintal while M-30 rose by 20/25 rupees to 1,230/1,395 rupees per quintal.
Sugar mill delivery climbed up by 5/10 rupees at 1,215/1,235 rupees per quintal.
Dealers said the free sale quota for May wast 750,000 tonnes, and June 800,000 tonnes.
Earlier traders were expecting a quota of 800,000 tonnes for May and 825,000 tonnes for June.
Generally sugar consumption goes up during the summer season when higher quotas are expected but the announcement of lower quotas prompted buoyancy in the market and sentiments were firm.
